'''Louis Victoire Athanase Dupré''' (28 December 1808 &ndash; 10 August 1869) was a French mathematician and physicist noted for his 1860s publications on the [[mechanical theory of heat]] ([[thermodynamics]]); work that was said to have inspired the publications of engineer [[François Massieu]] and his [[Massieu function]]s; which in turn inspired the work of American engineer [[Willard Gibbs]] and his [[fundamental equation]]s.
